newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt settles NZ$40 mln Maori land claim.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt settles NZ$40 mln Maori land claim.

text.p: New Zealand Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham said on Monday the government had agreed to settle a land claim by the Whakatohea Maori tribe for about NZ$40 million.
Graham said in a radio interview the settlement with the tribe, from the North Island's Bay of Plenty region, was mostly cash, but included a small amount of Crown land.
It would be officially signed on Tuesday.
Graham said it would be full and final, but he would not release details until the Whakatohea had briefed their people.
He said the settlement included a small amount of Crown land but no conservation land.
"The land taken from Whakatohea was about 170,000 acres. They did lose other land in various ways, but even if that were included it would not get within the range of the Tainui."
Graham said the Waikato-Tainui claim, settled for $170 million in land and cash last year, related to some one million acres of confiscated land.
The New Zealand government is also trying to settle the Ngai Tahu claim in the South Island before the October 12 election. It is expected to rival the Tainui claim.
Asked if any more settlements would be announced soon, Graham said: "We will know shortly".
